channel.title: whataifound.org: What AI Has Actually Contributed
channel.description: New and updated entries in the whataifound.org registry of AI contributions to science and mathematics, graded on verification and autonomy.

item.title: Bounds for higher-dimensional twisted paraproducts in the full open Banach range, machine-checked in Lean
item.description: Polona Durcik and Joris Roos register a Lean proof, generated with GPT-6.2 Astra Ultra and formalized with GPT-6.2 Sol Light, that the d-linear twisted paraproduct with a Mihlin-Hörmander multiplier is bounded from L^p₁ × ⋯ × L^p_d to Lᵖ for every d ≥ 2 and every exponent in the open Banach range, where no bounds at all were known for d ≥ 4. The operator integrates the product of the Fourier transforms of d functions on ℝᵈ against a multiplier that sees only the j-th coordinate of the j-th frequency, a twisted structure that defeats the standard time-frequency methods. Kovač proved the two-dimensional case for target exponents p < 2 in 2012, and Durcik and Roos proved a partial range in dimension three in 2021, writing then that nothing was known for d ≥ 4. The theorem gives, for 1 < p, pᵢ < ∞ with 1/p = ∑1/pᵢ, a constant C and an order s with ‖Tₘ(f₁, …, f_d)‖ₚ ≤ C[m]ₛ∏‖fᵢ‖_pᵢ for Schwartz inputs, so it also completes the Banach range in dimensions two and three. The development builds on Roos's lean-spherical library of harmonic analysis prerequisites. Lab: Independent. Model: GPT-6.2 Astra Ultra (proof and formalization blueprint); GPT-6.2 Sol Light (Lean formalization). Verification: Formally verified. Autonomy: AI-led.

item.title: First letters read in both halves of the Herculaneum scroll PHerc. 846
item.description: Vesuvius Challenge contestants using machine-learning ink detection revealed readable Greek letters in both surviving halves of PHerc. 846, a carbonised scroll in the National Library of Naples, including the sequence the challenge's papyrologists read as "of this man" and the word "citizen", earning two First Letters Prizes. PHerc. 846 is a whole scroll about 6 cm across and 22 cm tall that survives in two pieces, scanned separately as 846A and 846B. In 846B Brian Koenders found 15 certainly readable characters across several lines using a good segment and the public reader-v3 model; the papyrology team reads a sequence as a form of hapanta, all things, and later submissions on the same area added polites, citizen, and probably prosdokian, expectation. In the more compressed 846A, Jeff and David Chen unwrapped segments by hand, built labels iteratively and ran an ensemble of three models, and the team reads toutou anthropou, of this man, with diathesis, disposition, possible in the next line. The letter forms let the team place 846A as the lower and 846B as the upper part of the scroll and confirm the two belong together; the hand is dated provisionally to the 1st century BCE or CE. Lab: Vesuvius Challenge. Model: Domenico Russo's released reader-v3 ink model (846B); a z-score ensemble of a reader-v3 finetune, a v8-in finetune and the contestants' own HercUeNet model (846A). Verification: Author verified. Autonomy: AI-assisted.

item.title: Tao's 2024 MathOverflow question on relations in a Lie subalgebra, answered affirmatively
item.description: A 17-page preprint proves that the three obvious families of relations generate all relations of the Lie subalgebra Terence Tao asked about on MathOverflow in 2024, and finds that part of it is a free Lie algebra, with Codex and Claude used for literature search, computational experiments, verification code and drafting. Let g be the Lie algebra over a field of characteristic 0 generated by Dᵢ, Eᵢ subject to [Dᵢ, Dⱼ] = [Eᵢ, Eⱼ] = 0 and [Dᵢ, Eⱼ] = [Dⱼ, Eᵢ], and h the subalgebra generated by the [Dᵢ, Eⱼ] and the Eᵢ. Tao asked whether the relations [Dᵢ, Eⱼ] = [Dⱼ, Eᵢ], [Eᵢ, Eⱼ] = 0 and [Eᵢ, [Dⱼ, Eₖ]] = [Eₖ, [Dⱼ, Eᵢ]] generate all relations of h. The proof reduces to multilinear components by polarisation, presents the ideal generated by the Eᵢ, and uses a filtration whose associated graded algebra it computes to reduce injectivity to an equality of dimensions, which follows from a Hilbert series of g given by Eulerian numbers. By-products: h is a semidirect product of a free Lie algebra and an abelian one, and the [Dᵢ, Eⱼ] with i ≤ j freely generate a free Lie subalgebra. Lab: Independent. Model: OpenAI Codex and Anthropic Claude; versions not recorded. Verification: Claimed. Autonomy: AI-assisted.

item.title: Rohrbach's 1937 conjecture on thin bases of finite groups, proved in a weighted form
item.description: Yong Yang proves that for each h every finite group G has a subset A with Aʰ = G and |A| at most a constant times |G|^(1/h), as Rohrbach asked in 1937, and acknowledges that ChatGPT was used for mathematical exploration and editorial assistance. An h-basis of a finite group is a subset whose h-fold product set is the whole group, so it has at least |G|^(1/h) elements, and Rohrbach asked whether one within a constant factor of that always exists. The case h = 2 was known for all finite groups, Jia proved the conjecture for nilpotent groups and Kozma and Lev proved a stronger weighted form for solvable and alternating groups, with an extension lemma that reduces the problem to finite simple groups. The paper proves the weighted form with one absolute constant for every finite simple group of Lie type, by Singer-cycle transversals for the linear groups, a Bruhat transversal for the other classical families treated case by case, and separate arguments for the exceptional groups, which completes the program and answers the Modified Rohrbach Problem of Babai, Gál, Kimmel and Lokam. Lab: Texas State University. Model: OpenAI ChatGPT; version not stated. Verification: Author verified. Autonomy: AI-assisted.

item.title: Petty's polar projection conjecture claimed settled in dimension three and above, with the final step credited to GPT-6 Astra
item.description: A five-page preprint claims that in every dimension n ≥ 3 the polar projection body of a convex body is a dilate of it only when the body is an origin-centred ellipsoid, settling a 1971 question of Petty, and its provenance statement says the final key derivation and ideas were completed by AI. The projection body ΠK of a convex body K has support function given by the volumes of the hyperplane projections of K, and Petty asked whether TK = (ΠK)^(∘) being a positive dilate of K characterises ellipsoids. The preprint also covers the weaker condition that T²K is a dilate of K. Its argument is a distributional Laplacian identity that compares two integrals of central section volumes; equality forces contractive hyperplane projections in every kernel direction, and James's theorem on inner products in normed spaces then gives an ellipsoid. It states that the same argument proves the translative constant volume conjecture of Horváth and Lángi. Lab: Independent. Model: GPT-6 Astra (OpenAI ChatGPT). Verification: Claimed. Autonomy: Collaborative.

item.title: Lusztig's Fourier matrix conjecture for noncrystallographic Coxeter groups, claimed by a computer-assisted proof
item.description: A 37-page preprint posted with no claim of ownership gives a computer-assisted proof that for every finite noncrystallographic Coxeter group the normalized S-matrix of the Drinfeld center of each asymptotic Hecke category equals Lusztig's Fourier matrix, including the exact 74 by 74 identity for the middle cell of type H₄, with GPT-6 Pro used to develop and check it. For crystallographic Weyl groups the center of the asymptotic Hecke category is related to unipotent character sheaves, and Lusztig proposed in 2015 that the same construction should supply the missing categories for noncrystallographic groups, with modular matrices equal to the Fourier matrices constructed earlier by Lusztig, Malle and Broué. Elias and Williamson established the Soergel construction with its pivotal structure, and Rogel and Thiel proved the assertion for the dihedral groups and several cells of H₃ and H₄, leaving the 74-element family of the middle cell of H₄. The preprint fixes the pivotal signs by a relative Hodge-Riemann argument, builds a Morita equivalence for that cell with a crossed product of the Fibonacci Hecke category of type A₃, computes its whole Drinfeld center, and converts a certified numerical comparison into an exact equality of all 5,476 entries with a cyclotomic separation bound; the computations are in exact arithmetic over ℚ(√5) and certified complex balls. Lab: Independent. Model: GPT-6 Pro (OpenAI). Verification: Claimed. Autonomy: Collaborative.

item.title: Any-dimensional nonnegativity of symmetric functions is undecidable, and Hilbert's 17th problem has no uniform analogue
item.description: Two Konstanz mathematicians prove that it is undecidable whether a symmetric function with rational coefficients is nonnegative in every number of variables, and give an octic symmetric function that is positive definite in every dimension but has no sum-of-squares multiplier uniform in the dimension, writing that GPT 6.0 Astra found the initial proofs of both results. A symmetric function in the power sums p₁, p₂, … restricts to a polynomial in every number of variables, and Acevedo, Blekherman, Debus and Riener asked whether nonnegativity in all dimensions is decidable. The paper maps each integer polynomial P to an even homogeneous symmetric function that is nonnegative in all dimensions exactly when P has no zero in the natural numbers, so undecidability follows from Hilbert's tenth problem, and by the authors' account it makes the validity of dimension-free moment criteria for entanglement undecidable too. The second result is the explicit octic F = 4p₁²(p₃ − 4p₁³)² + 9p₂(p₆ − 8p₁²p₄ + 16p₁⁴p₂) − 16p₁⁸, positive definite in every dimension, for which any sum-of-squares multiplier must grow in degree with the dimension, so Artin's solution of Hilbert's 17th problem and the Krivine-Stengle Positivstellensatz have no dimension-free version. Lab: University of Konstanz. Model: GPT 6.0 Astra (OpenAI) for the initial proofs; Claude Fable 5.1 (Anthropic) in checking; coding agents for the Lean formalization. Verification: Author verified. Autonomy: AI-led.

item.title: A second AI-generated proof of the Courtade-Kumar conjecture, in OpenAI's math release, with a Lean statement
item.description: OpenAI's October 2026 math release includes a manuscript, credited to an unreleased internal model with no human author, proving that no Boolean function of uniform bits passed through binary symmetric noise carries more than 1 − h₂(ε) bits about the noisy output, as Courtade and Kumar conjectured, together with a sharper bound for biased functions and a Lean statement checked by Comparator. The manuscript, dated 24 September 2026, proves a sharp contraction for arbitrary soft binary channels u on the uniform cube: at a fixed initial information I(u), noise with correlation ρ reduces it at least as fast as it reduces a single noisy coordinate, and coordinates attain equality. The Boolean case gives the Courtade-Kumar inequality, and keeping the output entropy gives a curve strictly below 1 − h₂(ε) for nonconstant biased functions; a third theorem is a mean-dependent entropy-production bound. It follows the local-to-global differential program of Chen, Gohari and Nair, solving an arbitrary-mean joining problem with an explicit three-point optimizer, two entropy capacities and a common-output thinning inequality, then lifting by induction on dimension and integrating along the noise semigroup. The Lean scope note for family 119 links Comparator statements for the inequality with attainment and for the soft-channel contraction. Lab: OpenAI. Model: Unreleased internal OpenAI model, not named in the release. Verification: Claimed. Autonomy: AI-led.

item.title: Pointwise convergence of multiple ergodic averages of every length for mixing transformations, in OpenAI's math release
item.description: A manuscript in OpenAI's October 2026 math release, credited to an unreleased internal model with no human author, proves that for every invertible mixing measure-preserving transformation T and bounded functions f₁, …, fₙ, the averages N⁻¹∑_(k ≤ N)∏ⱼfⱼ(Tʲᵏx) converge almost everywhere to the product of the integrals, for every length n. Since Furstenberg's ergodic proof of Szemerédi's theorem these averages have been central to ergodic Ramsey theory. Host and Kra, and Ziegler, proved convergence in L² for every length, but almost-everywhere convergence was known only for two functions (Bourgain) and for longer averages under extra structure: K-systems, weakly mixing systems with restrictions on spectrum or joinings, and Huang, Shao and Ye's distal systems. The manuscript, dated 4 October 2026, needs neither a standard probability space nor a mixing rate. It passes to a suspension flow, builds probability laws from measurably chosen bad averaging lengths, and keeps a three-group independence structure as the number of factors grows, by minimising the number of slots carrying a nonzero centred correlation and using an energy-increment extension adapted from a companion fourfold result. It takes two other release results as inputs: that ordinary mixing implies mixing of all orders, Rokhlin's problem, and an oscillation estimate for triple averages at distinct slopes. Lab: OpenAI. Model: Unreleased internal OpenAI model, not named in the release. Verification: Claimed. Autonomy: AI-led.

item.title: No-go theorem for high-dimensional photonic GHZ states from pair sources, proof found by AlphaProof Nexus
item.description: A Lean proof found by Google DeepMind's AlphaProof Nexus agent shows that no complex-weighted monochromatic quantum graph exists on an even number N ≥ 4 of vertices with N colours, so photonic Greenberger-Horne-Zeilinger states of N photons in N or more dimensions cannot be made this way from probabilistic pair sources; six researchers have now explained the proof in a preprint. In the graph picture of photonic experiments, vertices are photon paths, coloured and weighted edges are photon pairs, and conditioning on one photon per detector turns each output amplitude into a coherent sum over perfect matchings. A GHZ state of N photons in D dimensions then corresponds to a monochromatic quantum graph, one whose matchings cancel on every non-monochromatic colouring and give equal weight to the D monochromatic ones. The 2017 conjecture of Krenn and Gu bounds the achievable D; earlier results covered nonnegative weights (Bogdanov), graphs without bichromatic edges or multi-edges, and sparse or cubic graphs. The proof builds a weighted sum of amplitudes whose coefficients factor vertex by vertex, so summing over the colours at one vertex reduces the system to an (N − 1) × N matrix of effective edge weights, whose row and column imbalance makes the sum vanish on any graph but not on the GHZ target. Since a graph for more than N colours restricts to one for N, the preprint states the result for every D ≥ N. Lab: Google DeepMind, with the University of Tübingen. Model: AlphaProof Nexus (Google DeepMind). Verification: Formally verified. Autonomy: Search scaffold.

item.title: Lean-checked 81/29 bound for Tuza's triangle-cover conjecture
item.description: AI research agents built and directed by Tyler B. Hughes proved, and formalized in Lean against a statement that uses only Mathlib, that every finite simple graph G satisfies τ(G) ≤ (81/29) ν(G), where ν is the largest number of edge-disjoint triangles and τ the fewest edges meeting every triangle, improving the bound of 165/59 posted by Sichen Wang in September 2026. Tuza conjectured in 1981 that τ(G) ≤ 2ν(G) for every graph, which would be sharp for K₄. The general bound stood at Haxell's 66/23 ≈ 2.870 from 1999 until 2026, when Yi lowered it to 63/22 in August and Wang to 165/59 ≈ 2.797 on 12 September, with a Lean formalization. The new bound is 81/29 ≈ 2.793. The Lean project extends Wang's MIT-licensed tuza-lean library with what its abstract calls helper-arborescence coupling, unmerged coloured-family covers and opposite-edge elimination. The challenge file is 101 lines, imports only Mathlib's clique, rational and lattice modules, and defines ν and τ as a supremum over triangle packings and an infimum over triangle transversals; it states the bound in natural-number form (29τ ≤ 81ν), in rational form and as the existence of a small transversal, together with the non-vacuity checks ν(K₄) = 1 and τ(K₄) = 2. A 32-vertex companion gadget is checked separately in exact rational Python and is not part of the theorem. The result is one of 41 that mathdiscoveries.org lists, each marked as not yet refereed by a human. Lab: Independent (mathdiscoveries.org). Model: AI research agents built by Tyler B. Hughes; the underlying models are not named. Verification: Formally verified. Autonomy: AI-led.

item.title: Lean-checked rhombic parallelohedron with ten faces in every zone, answering Grünbaum's question at k = 10
item.description: DICTO found a nonconvex polyhedron of 30 congruent golden rhombi, the rhombic triacontahedron less four oblate golden rhombohedra, in which every zone has exactly ten faces and whose lattice translates tile space face to face, and Claude Code wrote a Lean proof of these properties, giving an example for k = 10 of the question Grünbaum posed in 2010. In the Mathematical Intelligencer in 2010, Grünbaum asked, for each even k ≥ 4, whether some rhombic monohedral parallelohedron has exactly k faces in every zone, and wrote that no information was available for any k ≥ 10. The witness, which DICTO calls the Grünbaum-Escher triacontahedron GET B, is a union of 16 golden rhombohedra with 30 faces, 32 vertices and 60 edges. The Lean proof checks exact data in ℤ[φ] by kernel evaluation (zones, congruence of the faces, separating normals, contacts, face matching and cone separation from an interior point) and derives the tiling from the equality of volume and covolume using Mathlib's fundamental domains. Two calibration theorems check that the zone definition gives 4 for the cube and 6 for the rhombic dodecahedron. Since GET B is an indentation of the triacontahedron, it is also a counterexample to Grünbaum's tentative remark in the same paper that none of the other isozonohedra obtainable by indenting it seem to be parallelohedra. A paper is deposited on Zenodo. Lab: Independent (DICTO). Model: Claude Code with Claude Opus (Anthropic); version not stated. Verification: Formally verified. Autonomy: AI-assisted.

item.title: Sharp ionization bounds for helium and lithium, with mostly AI-generated proofs
item.description: Three Stanford researchers prove in the nonrelativistic Coulomb model that a helium nucleus binds at most two electrons and a lithium nucleus at most four, both sharp, improving Lieb's 1984 bound N_c(Z) < 2Z + 1 for these nuclei; they say the ideas were mostly human and the proofs in this version mostly AI-generated. The ionization problem asks for the largest number N_c(Z) of electrons a nucleus of charge Z can bind. Lieb's bound is sharp for hydrogen but allows four electrons for helium and six for lithium, and later asymptotic and explicit improvements did not lower those limits; Shelley and Tartakovsky had earlier excluded the helium dianion, lowering helium to three. The paper shows N_c(2) = 2 and N_c(3) = 4, so the helium anion and the lithium dianion are not bound, while the lithium anion is. The main tool is an adaptation of Lieb's argument with a quadratic weight, which reduces the nonbinding of the doubly negative ions to finitely many inequalities verified in a computer-assisted proof, with about fifty pages of geometric, radial and integral certificates in the appendices and code on Zenodo. Lab: Stanford University. Model: Fable and Astra, run in the Pharos harness built on Rethlas; versions not stated. Verification: Claimed. Autonomy: Collaborative.

item.title: Proof of Euler's 1747 conjecture on sums of two integers with prime factors 1 mod 4, drafted by OpenAI Codex
item.description: Four Purdue researchers prove that every positive integer n ≡ 2 (mod 4) is a sum of two positive integers whose prime factors are all ≡ 1 (mod 4), with 1 allowed, as Euler proposed to Goldbach in 1747, and say that OpenAI Codex generated the argument, performed the exact calculations and drafted the manuscript under their direction. Euler stated the assertion in a letter to Goldbach of 6 May 1747. Dietmann and Elsholtz proved in 2019 that it holds for every sufficiently large n, without an explicit threshold. The new proof counts all representations of n by four squares and bounds those in which a prime p ≡ 3 (mod 4) divides both coordinates of either pair; an average over a nonsplit torus normalizer turns the quaternionic Hecke bound, available through Jacquet-Langlands and Deligne, into an error independent of the sieving prime, and elementary estimates then give the explicit threshold 64⁴ = 16,777,216. An exact arithmetic certificate covers the 4,194,304 integers in the residue class below it, by a sieve whose counts the paper tabulates. Lab: Purdue University. Model: OpenAI Codex; version not stated. Verification: Claimed. Autonomy: AI-led.

item.title: Finiteness of strongly reflective modular forms, answering Borcherds and Gritsenko–Nikulin, with AI used in parts of the proof
item.description: Two Wuhan University mathematicians prove that up to conjugation and scaling there are only finitely many strongly reflective modular forms on orthogonal groups of signature (n, 2) with n at least 3, settling a 1998 conjecture of Gritsenko and Nikulin and answering a question Borcherds posed in 1995; they say they used generative AI interactively to develop, test and refine parts of the proof after building the framework themselves. A modular form on an orthogonal arithmetic group is strongly reflective if its zero divisor is a reduced union of mirrors of reflections in the group. Such forms, often Borcherds products, are tied to reflective lattices, hyperbolic reflection groups and generalized Kac-Moody algebras. The paper proves finiteness up to conjugation and scaling, and more generally for reflective forms whose mirror multiplicities are bounded by any fixed m (its Theorem 1.3); as consequences it gets the finiteness of holomorphic automorphic products of singular weight and of the groups whose algebra of modular forms is freely generated. The key ingredient is a uniform upper bound on the covolume of the group, obtained by adapting the higher-rank lattice convergence theorem of Abért and coauthors, on invariant random subgroups, to the degrees of reflective branch divisors. Lab: Wuhan University. Model: Generative AI; not named. Verification: Claimed. Autonomy: AI-assisted.

item.title: Routine EHR models predict three of seven pregnancy complications in the first trimester, and lose accuracy on transfer
item.description: Gradient-boosted models trained on 442,760 Kaiser Permanente Northern California pregnancies predicted gestational hypertension, gestational diabetes and pre-eclampsia at 12 weeks with AUCs of 0.789, 0.800 and 0.740 from routine records alone, but four birth outcomes stayed between 0.62 and 0.68, and on 6,105 All of Us pregnancies the models needed local tuning to approach their home performance. The study trained separate models every six weeks of gestation for seven outcomes on pregnancies from 2011 to 2021, using only routinely collected diagnoses, vital signs, laboratory tests and medications. At 24 weeks preterm birth, stillbirth, placental abruption and small for gestational age reached AUCs of 0.683, 0.667, 0.622 and 0.654, which the authors call limited for intervention. Every complication had an incidence below 10%, two below 2%. A cost-effectiveness analysis paired model-based risk stratification with evidence-based interventions for the three predictable conditions. In the All of Us cohort, where the last menstrual period was unavailable and delivery date minus 40 weeks was used instead, the transferred models trailed the KPNC test data by an average of 12.9 AUC points untuned, 8.8 with 20% local fine-tuning and 8.5 with 50%. Code is public, with synthetic data for the KPNC pipeline. Lab: MIT and Kaiser Permanente Northern California. Model: XGBoost gradient-boosted trees, one per complication and gestational week. Verification: Peer reviewed. Autonomy: AI-assisted.

item.title: Proof of the Theta conjecture and the valley Delta conjecture, developed with ChatGPT and checked in Lean
item.description: Five mathematicians at Nankai University prove the touching refinement of the Theta conjecture of Interdonato and Iraci, and with it the valley version of the Delta conjecture of Haglund, Remmel and Wilson, saying the derivations and proofs were developed with ChatGPT 6 Astra; a separate Lean proof written with OpenAI Codex checks the main theorem and the Theta conjecture against a statement that imports only Mathlib. The Delta conjecture gives a combinatorial formula for a Delta operator applied to eₙ in terms of decorated labelled Dyck paths, in a rise and a valley version; the rise version has been proved, while the valley version remained open. D'Adderio and coauthors introduced the Theta operators, and Interdonato and Iraci conjectured a formula for Θ_e_ℓΘ_eₖ∇e_d as a sum over parking functions carrying both decorated rises and decorated contractible valleys, which contains both versions, together with a refinement by the touch number. The paper proves the refinement (its Theorem 1.4) by comparing an algebraic recurrence, from an endomorphism of the Dyck path algebra of Carlsson and Mellit, with a combinatorial one obtained by introducing signed labels and deleting the main diagonal. Summing over the touch number gives the Theta conjecture, and the corollaries give the valley Delta conjecture and the generalized valley Delta conjecture of Qiu and Wilson. The Lean repository states ten results in a challenge file that imports only Mathlib and defines the modified Macdonald polynomials by Haiman's characterization, the operators and the decorated parking functions itself; the 849-module proof follows a different route from the manuscript, through a recursion in a polynomial model of the Dyck path algebra. Lab: Nankai University. Model: ChatGPT 6 Astra (OpenAI) for the manuscript; OpenAI Codex for the Lean library. Verification: Formally verified. Autonomy: AI-assisted.

item.title: First-in-human phase 1 results for ISM6331, a pan-TEAD inhibitor designed with Insilico's Chemistry42
item.description: Insilico Medicine reported at ESMO 2026 that four of 22 evaluable patients with previously treated mesothelioma had partial responses to ISM6331, an oral pan-TEAD inhibitor designed with its Chemistry42 generative chemistry software, with no dose-limiting toxicities between 15 and 130 mg in the ongoing dose-escalation study. TEAD proteins work with YAP and TAZ to switch on growth genes that the Hippo pathway normally restrains, and defects in that pathway, such as loss of NF2, are common in mesothelioma. ISM6331 blocks palmitoylation of all four TEAD family members. In the phase 1 part of NCT06566079, as presented by Melina Marmarelis of the University of Pennsylvania with an August 2026 data cutoff and reported by Drug Discovery and Development, the response rate in mesothelioma was 18.2% and disease control at the first scan 68.2%, with three of four responses ongoing and one lasting about a year; at 130 mg, the highest dose reported, two of five evaluable patients responded. Patients had a median of two prior lines of therapy. Across 36 patients with mesothelioma or other solid tumours, four had grade 1 or 2 reversible proteinuria, an on-target class effect, and three at 130 mg had grade 3 treatment-related events. Insilico plans a randomized phase 2a dose-optimization study in 2027. Lab: Insilico Medicine. Model: Chemistry42 (Insilico Medicine). Verification: Claimed. Autonomy: Search scaffold.

item.title: Gauge-invariant lattice measure for chiral fermions including the Standard Model, with an Astra-led proof
item.description: Nathaniel Craig constructs a smooth, gauge-invariant measure for overlap fermions on four-dimensional Euclidean lattices for a class of nonabelian chiral gauge theories that includes the Standard Model, giving a candidate nonperturbative lattice definition of it, and writes that OpenAI's GPT-6 Astra was essential and that the current proof is Astra-led. Left- and right-handed fermions carry different gauge charges in the weak interactions, and no lattice regulator respecting both gauge invariance and chiral symmetry has been known for nonabelian chiral theories in four dimensions, so the Standard Model has lacked a nonperturbative definition. Overlap fermions with Lüscher's reconstruction theorem settled the abelian case. Here the measure current is built by comparing chiral projectors at successive lattice spacings: a smooth connection is reconstructed locally from the links on admissible gauge fields and sampled on finer lattices, and the paper proves the current is exponentially local and satisfies the integrability conditions Lüscher's reconstruction needs, then restricts to the four possible global forms of the Standard Model gauge group. Verification is described on three fronts: a Lean formalization of the mathematical companion (sixteen modules, standard axioms, kernel replay), an analogous two-dimensional construction compared numerically with determinant phases, and a second construction in the opposite order that agrees up to local counterterms. Lab: UC Santa Barbara, with OpenAI. Model: GPT-6 Astra (OpenAI). Verification: Claimed. Autonomy: Collaborative.

item.title: Proof of the Courtade–Kumar most informative Boolean function conjecture, mostly AI-generated and checked in Lean
item.description: Researchers at Google and the Chinese University of Hong Kong give a computer-assisted proof, verified end to end in Lean, that no Boolean function of n bits sent through a binary symmetric channel carries more than 1 − h(α) bits of mutual information with the noisy output, the value attained by a dictator, and write that the overwhelming majority of the new ideas and results were generated by AI. Courtade and Kumar conjectured in 2013 that for X uniform on {0, 1}ⁿ and Y obtained by flipping each bit independently with probability α, every Boolean f satisfies I(f(X);Y) ≤ 1 − h(α), where h is binary entropy, and verified it numerically up to dimension seven. The proof builds on the differential-equation method of the CUHK group, which reduces the problem to a finite-dimensional optimization given the right Bellman candidate function: differentiation along the noise semigroup writes entropy production as an average of edge costs, and the key estimate becomes an unrestricted Bellman inequality with two mean and two entropy constraints. Part 1 proves the balanced case and Part 2 the unbalanced one, with validated interval arithmetic for the computational lemmas. The Lean project has about 45,500 modules and needed roughly 1,200 CPU-hours to check; its 63-line statement file is also in Google DeepMind's Formal Conjectures repository. Lab: Google, with the Chinese University of Hong Kong. Model: Gemini 4 Argon and earlier Gemini models (Google DeepMind), in the Stellar Colosseum framework; Anthropic and OpenAI models also contributed. Verification: Formally verified. Autonomy: Collaborative.

item.title: Lean proof of the Riemann hypothesis and GRH for Dirichlet L-functions, released without a paper
item.description: Levent Alpöge, a mathematician at Anthropic, says he found with Claude a proof that every nontrivial zero of the Riemann zeta function, and of every Dirichlet L-function, has real part one half, and has released it only as a Lean formalization of about 17 million lines that he says he does not yet fully understand. Riemann conjectured in 1859 that every nontrivial zero of ζ(s) has real part 1/2, and the generalized Riemann hypothesis makes the same assertion for Dirichlet L-functions. The release is a Lean 4 project and a four-page note, with no paper. Its Main.lean proves riemannHypothesis, whose type is Mathlib's own RiemannHypothesis (which excludes the trivial zeros and the point s = 1), together with four companion theorems: no Dirichlet L-function vanishes in ℜs > 1/2, for every modulus and every character, imprimitive ones included, with the pole of the principal character at s = 1 excepted; and every zero of one with 0 < ℜs < 1 lies on ℜs = 1/2, stated again separately for primitive characters. The project pins Lean 4.33.1 and Mathlib's v4.33.1 tag and runs to 175,187 files and about 17.4 million lines, with no comments and 818,755 theorem or lemma declarations, every file in the import closure of Main. RH itself is derived from the nonvanishing of all Dirichlet L-functions to the right of 1/2 by the standard functional-equation argument, using Mathlib's lemmas. The note gives the strategy only in outline. The argument descends from Stepanov's method for the Riemann hypothesis over function fields, where a divisor with multiplicity does the work; over the integers multiplicity would be something like differentiating whole numbers, and it is imitated instead by a chain of theta lifts between totally definite unitary groups, a chain of m lifts winning multiplicity m. For a von Mangoldt sum of length X the chain is taken about √X long, a choice the note attributes to Claude. Other ingredients it names include Gan-Gross-Prasad periods, a relative trace formula, an Iwasawa tower, the Bost slope inequality and a weakening of Vandiver's conjecture. A timeline the note says Claude reconstructed puts the first step, a Stepanov-type determinant, on 6 October 2026 and GRH on 16 November 2026. Lab: Anthropic. Model: Claude (Anthropic); version not stated, described by Terence Tao as an internal model. Verification: Formally verified. Autonomy: Collaborative.

item.title: Harmonic's Aristotle finds a rounding bug while formally verifying Manifest's Solana order book
item.description: Harmonic reports that its Aristotle system proved 28 properties of Manifest's open-source Rust order book on Solana and found two defects, including a rounding case in which a complete fill overshooting its target returned an arithmetic error; Manifest's fix, merged on 8 October 2026, cites the finding. Manifest's quote function computes how much base token a trader gets for a given amount of quote token. Rounding can make a fill overshoot the remaining target: at a price of 1.5, one base atom costs two quote atoms even when one is still needed. The original code stopped early only on a partial fill, so a complete fill went on to subtract two from one and returned arithmetic error 14 after the target had been met. Manifest's pull request 751, merged on 8 October 2026, makes the walk stop once a complete fill meets or exceeds the target 'as recommended by Manifest FV Report V2 finding 2.1', and notes that only the exact-out-quote swap path could hit it. Harmonic's case study says the second finding was an unused quote conversion on the global-order cancel path that could fail before the order was removed, also fixed, and that Aristotle reasoned over the unchanged Rust with no simplified model, proving trading progress, error classification, order-book integrity, custody and matching properties. Lab: Harmonic. Model: Aristotle. Verification: Claimed. Autonomy: AI-assisted.

item.title: Deep learning on routine chest radiographs predicts major osteoporotic fractures better than FRAX
item.description: A convolutional survival model trained on 53,109 adults at a Korean tertiary hospital and validated on 85,284 patients from two other institutions predicted incident major osteoporotic fracture from routine chest radiographs with a C-index of 0.843, against 0.779 for FRAX with bone density. Bone density and FRAX miss much of the fracture risk in the osteopenic range, where most fractures occur. Participants needed a chest radiograph within a year of a DXA scan. In the external cohorts (mean age 58.6, 68.9% female, 77 months of follow-up) the model reached a C-index of 0.843 (95% CI 0.837 to 0.850) and a censoring-adjusted 10-year AUROC of 0.855, against 0.779 and 0.785 for FRAX with BMD (both P < 0.01); adding FRAX to the model barely changed it (C-index 0.847). In the osteopenia subgroup of 35,358 patients the 10-year AUROC was 0.779 against 0.659, and the advantage held across fracture types and BMD categories. The study was funded by the National Research Foundation of Korea and others. Lab: Seoul National University Hospital. Model: A convolutional neural network survival model; not named. Verification: Peer reviewed. Autonomy: AI-assisted.

item.title: Sharp logarithmic Kakeya maximal and tube bounds in every dimension, registered as a Lean proof
item.description: Mark Lewko, with ChatGPT and Codex doing the mathematical development and Lean implementation, registered on Palomar a Lean proof that the Kakeya maximal operator is bounded from Lⁿ(ℝⁿ) to Lⁿ(S^(n − 1)) with norm at most Cₙ[log(2/δ)]^((n − 1)/n) in every dimension n ≥ 2, a logarithmic power the accompanying notes argue is optimal. For 0 < δ ≤ 1 the Kakeya maximal function takes the largest average of |f| over radius-δ neighbourhoods of unit segments in each direction. The two Lean theorems are the maximal bound ‖K_δf‖_(Lⁿ(S^(n − 1))) ≤ Cₙ[log(2/δ)]^((n − 1)/n)‖f‖_(Lⁿ(ℝⁿ)) and a weighted tube bound: for δ-separated directions, arbitrary centres and nonnegative weights, ∫(∑ⱼaⱼ1_Tⱼ)^(n/(n − 1)) ≤ Cₙlog(2/δ) δ^(n − 1)∑ⱼaⱼ^(n/(n − 1)). By Hölder's inequality the δ-neighbourhood of every Kakeya set then has volume at least cₙ/[log(2/δ)]^(n − 1), which matches the construction of Fernández-Delgado and de la Salle, and the estimates imply the Kakeya maximal function conjecture and full Minkowski dimension for every bounded Kakeya set. Those consequences and the matching lower bound are written arguments, not Lean theorems. The development reuses 1,682 files of OpenAI's Lean library at a pinned commit, which the record calls substantial reuse rather than an independent implementation of the analytic infrastructure. Lab: Independent. Model: OpenAI ChatGPT and Codex; versions not stated. Verification: Claimed. Autonomy: AI-assisted.

item.title: Kim's dimension inequality for curves over Q with a rational point, via noncommutative Iwasawa theory
item.description: Sa'ar Zehavi proves Kim's conjectured dimension inequality for every smooth projective curve of genus at least two over ℚ with a rational basepoint, at every odd prime of good reduction and all sufficiently large levels, so the Chabauty–Kim method works unconditionally for such curves; the key nontrivial bound was developed in a lengthy back-and-forth with GPT-6 Astra. Kim's method bounds rational points on a curve by comparing the étale and de Rham unipotent fundamental groups at level n; it yields finiteness whenever the Selmer dimension dim H_f¹(G_(ℚ, Σ), Uₙᵉᵗ) falls below dim(Uₙ^dR/F⁰), which Kim conjectured in 2009 always happens for large n. The paper proves this for every odd prime p of good reduction, with no restriction on the Jacobian's endomorphism ring or Galois image, by bounding second Galois cohomology through kernels of Iwasawa operators acting on representations of the generalized symplectic group, an approach the author traces to Coates and Kim's work on curves with CM Jacobians. As a consequence the Chabauty–Kim loci are finite at large levels, recovering the Mordell conjecture over ℚ, Faltings's theorem, through Kim's method. Lab: Independent (Max Planck Institute for Mathematics). Model: GPT-6 Astra (OpenAI), Ultra mode. Verification: Claimed. Autonomy: Collaborative.

item.title: Automorphic realization of Langlands parameters for split groups over function fields, Part I
item.description: A single-author Hexagon preprint, whose mathematical arguments its provenance statement says were developed with GPT-6 Astra Pro, claims the converse to V. Lafforgue's decomposition: every semisimple elliptic Langlands parameter of a split reductive group over a global function field is the parameter of a cusp form, with this part's theorems resting on existence results deposited separately as Parts II and III. V. Lafforgue decomposed the space of cusp forms on a split connected reductive group G over a global function field F according to semisimple Langlands parameters. This is the first of three papers claiming the converse: every semisimple elliptic parameter is the parameter of a cusp form on G over F itself, in every positive characteristic for classical groups and above stated characteristic bounds for the exceptional groups (greater than 3 for G₂ and F₄, 5 for E₆, 7 for E₇ and E₈). Part I contains the arithmetic half: it defines excursion operators on functions not assumed cuspidal, proves compatibility with constant terms, and reduces the theorems to the existence of a cusp form with a given elliptic parameter on a simply connected simple group. That existence is proved in Part II by a geometric method and in Part III for classical groups by descent from general linear groups. Lab: Independent. Model: GPT-6 Astra Pro (mathematical arguments) and Claude Fable 5.2 (organizing and rewriting), per the provenance statement; the record's tools field lists GPT-6 Pro. Verification: Claimed. Autonomy: AI-led.

item.title: The coercivity conjecture for nonlocal energies fails whenever n > 2s, and holds in restricted classes
item.description: Six authors including Xavier Ros-Oton show that uniform ellipticity does not imply Hˢ-coercivity for symmetric nonlocal kernels of order 2s whenever n > 2s, while it does hold for n = 1 and s > 1/2 and for kernels with annular cancellation, after sustained interactions with ChatGPT versions 5.5, 5.6 and 6. The conjecture asks whether directional moment bounds on a symmetric kernel of order 2s, 0 < s < 1, imply coercivity in Hˢ; Imbert and Silvestre proposed it in a kinetic setting, where it bears on the divergence-form approach to the non-cutoff Boltzmann equation. The paper shows it fails whenever n > 2s, for every s and n ≥ 1, even for smooth compactly supported test functions, and holds for n = 1 and s > 1/2. The construction also gives bounded discontinuous weak solutions in H_locˢ to nonlocal equations in divergence form. On the positive side, a local coercivity criterion based on annular cancellation covers kernels with both divergence- and nondivergence-form symmetry, kernels comparable to stable kernels with bounded measurable coefficients, and non-cutoff Boltzmann kernels under a geometric nonconcentration assumption, and gives a short proof of the Gressman–Strain anisotropic coercivity estimate. Lab: Independent. Model: ChatGPT versions 5.5, 5.6 and 6. Verification: Claimed. Autonomy: AI-assisted.

item.title: Explicit restricted isometries with k = m^(2/3 − o(1)), first proved in one shot by GPT-6 Astra
item.description: Kümmerle and Mixon construct explicit real restricted isometry matrices whose sparsity level reaches k = m^(2/3 − o(1)), past the square-root barrier that conventional wisdom attached to proofs of this kind, on a problem Tao posed in 2007; their declaration says the main theorem was proved in one shot using GPT-6 Astra. A matrix has the restricted isometry property of order k when it nearly preserves the length of every k-sparse vector, which is what compressed sensing needs. Random matrices achieve k nearly proportional to m; Tao asked in 2007 for comparable explicit constructions, and the abstract notes the conventional wisdom that proofs using only the entrywise absolute value of the Gram matrix stall at m^(1/2). The paper combines Gershgorin's circle theorem with a flat RIP estimate to reduce the problem to choosing a large vertex set in a strongly regular graph in which every small subset spans few edges, and selects that set using an incidence result of Zahl. It also proves that methods using only the entrywise absolute value of the Gram matrix face a barrier at m^(2/3), not m^(1/2) as had been believed, and that this construction meets it. The authors write that while digesting the AI proof they distilled the Gershgorin and flat RIP hybrid, identified the 2/3 barrier and explored the general approach over several long conversations with ChatGPT. Lab: Independent. Model: GPT-6 Astra (main theorem); ChatGPT and Claude Opus 5.5 (exploration, drafting and feedback); an Opus 5.5 orchestrator with GPT-6.1 Sol and GPT-6 Astra subagents (Lean). Verification: Claimed. Autonomy: AI-led.

item.title: The Ideal Generation Conjecture for general reduced points in projective space, characteristic zero
item.description: A Hexagon preprint described as 'a guided exploration by Open AI Astra agents' proves that for general reduced points in projective space over an algebraically closed field of characteristic zero, multiplication by linear forms from the initial degree D of their ideal to degree D + 1 has maximal rank, and its main theorem is registered on Palomar as a Lean proof. For a general set of points in projective space, the Ideal Generation Conjecture predicts the minimal number of generators of their homogeneous ideal, equivalently that the multiplication map from the degree D part of the ideal tensored with linear forms to its degree D + 1 part has maximal rank. The paper's references include Geramita and Orecchia (1982), Geramita and Maroscia (1984), Hirschowitz and Simpson (1996), who settled the case of a large number of points, and Lauze (1995). The proof combines hyperplane specialization with a construction using two transverse hyperplanes, whose common trace moves to give the required rank, and a uniform induction for D ≥ 4 reduces everything to explicit quadratic and cubic constructions. The Palomar record formalizes Theorem 1.1 for every dimension n ≥ 1, degree D ≥ 2 and point count in the relevant range, and states that the ideal has exactly the predicted numbers of minimal generators in degrees D and D + 1 and is generated in those degrees. Lab: Independent. Model: OpenAI Astra agents; version not stated. Verification: Claimed. Autonomy: Collaborative.

item.title: Exact diameter of the symmetric group with LRX generators, n(n−1)/2 for every n ≥ 4
item.description: Seven authors report that their agentic system, mainly GPT-6 Astra, proved the undirected Cayley graph of Sₙ generated by the cyclic shift, its inverse and the transposition of the first two positions has diameter n(n − 1)/2 for every n ≥ 4, with a finite set of special cases checked by C++ code and the result registered on Palomar as a Lean proof. With L the cyclic shift, R = L⁻¹ and X the transposition of the first two positions, the question is the largest distance between two permutations in the Cayley graph, OEIS A186783; the paper says the conjectured value was open since at least 2011, and the CayleyPy growth computations listed it among their conjectures. The paper establishes sharp upper and lower bounds by combinatorial and group-theoretic arguments, leaving a finite set of special cases verified by accompanying C++ code. The Palomar record proves the upper and lower bounds and constructs an explicit L, R, X word of at most that length between every ordered pair of permutations, against a Mathlib-only Challenge. Lab: Independent. Model: GPT-6 Astra (agentic system and Codex); Claude Opus 5.5 (minor checks and editing). Verification: Claimed. Autonomy: AI-led.

item.title: The supercritical Ten Martini Problem, with an LLM used for the renormalization and KAM steps
item.description: Ge, Jitomirskaya and You prove Cantor spectrum on the positive-Lyapunov part of the spectrum of every nonconstant real analytic one-frequency Schrödinger operator, settling a 2024 conjecture of You; their appendix says they conceived the whole strategy without AI and then used an LLM to help carry out the renormalization and local KAM steps. The Ten Martini Problem asks whether the spectrum of a quasi-periodic Schrödinger operator is a Cantor set; for the almost Mathieu operator it was settled by Avila and Jitomirskaya. In the supercritical regime Cantor spectrum is expected for every nonconstant analytic potential and every irrational frequency, which You formulated as a conjecture in 2024. The paper proves it on the closure of the positive-Lyapunov part of the spectrum by using the intrinsic symplectic center of Ge and Jitomirskaya to extend the Kotani and almost reducibility arguments of Ge, Jitomirskaya and You from a two-dimensional center to one of arbitrary finite dimension. Appendix B states that the model helped derive the renormalization estimate of Lemma 5.1 and discover the monotonicity property of Lemma 3.2, and was 'particularly valuable' in using that property to simplify the authors' original local KAM argument with parameters. Lab: Independent. Model: An unnamed LLM. Verification: Claimed. Autonomy: AI-assisted.

item.title: A linear bound on zeros of polyanalytic polynomials, via a topological approach suggested by GPT-6.1
item.description: Lundberg, Rosen and Zhang prove that a complex polynomial of degree n in z and m < n in z̄ with finitely many zeros has at most (4m + 1)n − 5m of them, answering Eremenko's question of whether the count is linear in n for fixed m, using an approach through the Kronheimer–Mrowka theorem that GPT-6.1 suggested. The problem of bounding the zeros goes back to Sheil-Small, and known bounds for polynomials of this kind were quadratic in n; Eremenko asked whether, for each fixed m, the dependence can be made linear, generalizing open questions for particular subclasses. The paper bihomogenizes the polynomial, considers its zero curve, and applies the genus bound of Kronheimer and Mrowka from their proof of Thom's conjecture. It gives examples showing the bound is asymptotically sharp as n → ∞ for each fixed m; these examples are not harmonic, so they do not bear on the separate conjecture for harmonic polynomials. Lab: Independent. Model: GPT-6.1. Verification: Claimed. Autonomy: Collaborative.

item.title: The L'vov–Kaplansky conjecture for matrices of sufficiently large order
item.description: A Hexagon preprint whose main results were developed over ten GPT-6-Pro research runs claims that for each degree, the image of a nonzero multilinear polynomial on n × n matrices over any field is the traceless matrices or the whole matrix algebra, as the L'vov–Kaplansky conjecture predicts, once n exceeds a threshold depending only on the degree. The L'vov–Kaplansky conjecture, recorded in the Dniester Notebook, says the image of a multilinear polynomial evaluated on n × n matrices is always {0}, the scalars, the traceless matrices or the whole algebra. Prior work studied small cases, such as images on 2 × 2 and 3 × 3 matrices (Kanel-Belov, Malev and Rowen) and instances in degree three (Dykema and Klep, and later authors). The preprint claims the full dichotomy for every degree in all sizes beyond a degree-dependent threshold: the image is the traceless subspace if every cyclic coefficient sum vanishes, and the full matrix algebra otherwise. Lab: Independent. Model: GPT-6-Pro (ten research runs, 62.5 scheduled hours) and Codex (proof audit and manuscript polish). Verification: Claimed. Autonomy: AI-led.

item.title: Hawking–Page transition at weak coupling in N=4 super Yang–Mills is first order, computed by Claude
item.description: An Anthropic preprint reports that a Claude research model computed the three-loop quartic coefficient b = −1.48 × 10⁻³λ² in the Polyakov-loop effective action of N = 4 super Yang–Mills on S³, settling a question set up in 2003: the weak-coupling deconfinement transition is first order, like the Hawking–Page transition it is dual to. In anti-de Sitter space a black hole forms through a first-order phase transition found by Hawking and Page in 1983, which in N = 4 super Yang–Mills on S³ is deconfinement at strong coupling. The free theory has a transition at its Hagedorn temperature, and Aharony, Marsano, Minwalla, Papadodimas and Van Raamsdonk (hep-th/0310285) suggested in 2003 that the two could be connected either by a single first-order line or through a pair of continuous transitions at weak coupling, with the answer decided by the sign of a quartic coefficient b that first appears at three loops. The preprint reports b = −1.48 × 10⁻³λ², with λ the 't Hooft coupling, so the transition is first order and lies slightly below the Hagedorn temperature, with its three saddle points appearing, exchanging dominance and disappearing in the same order as thermal AdS and the small and large black holes. The computation is Hamiltonian, almost every number in it was obtained in two independent ways, and it reproduces the two-loop Hagedorn temperature known from integrability and exact results in closed subsectors. Lab: Anthropic. Model: An internal Claude research model; Anthropic's post presents the results under Claude Fable 5.2. Verification: Claimed. Autonomy: AI-led.

item.title: Exact large-c slope of the spinless modular bootstrap bound, found by Claude
item.description: An Anthropic preprint reports that a Claude research model found the exact optimal slope of the spinless modular bootstrap bound on the lightest primary in two-dimensional CFTs at large central charge, Λ_V = 12π²/(π² + 4 arcsinh²1) ≈ 9.1266, where it had been known only to lie between 8.503 and 12. The spinless modular bootstrap bounds the dimension Δ₁ of the lightest non-vacuum primary in a unitary compact 2D CFT with c > 1 and no extra conserved currents using only modular S invariance at zero angular potential, giving Δ₁ ≤ c/Λ + o(c). Hellerman's 2009 bound started this line, and the best slope was known to lie between 8.503 and 12, the latter being where the bound would reach the BTZ black hole threshold. The preprint shows the optimum is exactly Λ_V, that no functional in a class containing all finite combinations of derivatives improves on c/Λ_V by more than O(c^(1/3)log^(2/3) c), and gives an explicit functional with Δ₁ < c/Λ_V + 0.483 c^(1/3) + O(1). The value has an electrostatic origin: c⁻¹log|g| of a functional g is a two-dimensional potential with charges at its zeros, and the maximum principle bounds it by an explicit harmonic function. It also conjectures the coefficient of the c^(1/3) correction, supported by numerics up to c = 2048. Lab: Anthropic. Model: An internal Claude research model, later reproduced by Claude Opus 5.5; Anthropic's post presents the results under Claude Fable 5.2. Verification: Claimed. Autonomy: AI-led.

item.title: Cable knot counterexamples to the full-sequence volume conjecture for all knots
item.description: Haibin Hang, with OpenAI Codex assisting, shows that for the (1,2)-cable of the connected sum of two figure-eight knots the growth rate of the colored Jones polynomial does not converge along all colors, so the volume conjecture's full-sequence limit fails for knots in general, extending parity effects Lê and Tran found for cables in 2009. The volume conjecture says the normalized logarithmic growth of a knot's colored Jones polynomial at q = e^(2πi/N) tends to its simplicial volume times the volume of the regular ideal tetrahedron. For the (p, w)-cable of the connected sum of d ≥ 2 copies of the figure-eight knot E, with w ≥ 2 and p, w coprime, the paper shows the growth rate converges to the JSJ volume dV along colors coprime to 2w, while its upper limit along colors sharing a divisor with w is at most V. So the (1,2)-cable of E#E violates the full-sequence limit, and the (1,3)-cable shows convergence can fail even along all odd colors. The all-color upper limit still agrees with the JSJ volume. The separation comes from the multiples of N in the exact cabling sum and a uniform first-derivative estimate for the other companion colors. Lab: Independent. Model: OpenAI Codex; version not stated. Verification: Claimed. Autonomy: AI-assisted.

item.title: An ECG biomarker for sudden cardiac death, discovered with deep learning
item.description: Trained on every ECG in a Swedish region linked to death certificates, a deep learning model isolated 2.2% of patients with a 7.0% annual rate of sudden cardiac death, above the 4.6% of those flagged by reduced ejection fraction, and 86.1% of them were missed by that standard screen; a generative model then exposed the waveform feature it used, which the authors say had not been described. Defibrillators can prevent sudden cardiac death, but the only predictive marker in wide use, left ventricular ejection fraction, misses most such deaths and flags many low-risk patients for devices that never fire. The model's high-risk group (2.2% of the sample) had a 7.0% annual rate of sudden cardiac death against 4.6% for patients with reduced ejection fraction (1.9% of the sample), and high-risk ECG patients who had defibrillators implanted were 54.4% less likely to die than expected. The model was externally validated in a US health system, where it predicts the ventricular arrhythmias that cause sudden death, and in a Taiwanese hospital registry, where it predicts arrhythmic cardiac arrest. Pairing it with a generative model of the ECG waveform revealed the morphology it had learned, which the authors describe as easily visible, and they tie its shape to electrophysiological first principles to propose and preliminarily test a mechanism. Lab: UC Berkeley, with the University of Chicago, MIT and Halmstad University and Region Halland. Model: A deep learning model on 12-lead ECG waveforms, paired with a generative model of the waveform; not named. Verification: Peer reviewed. Autonomy: Search scaffold.

item.title: First lower bounds above n for Naslund's crossing problem, found and proved in Lean by an agent team
item.description: A multi-agent harness of Claude models run by Arth Singh proved in Lean, over every field, that the quantity P(n) in Naslund's crossing problem is at least 4n/3, then 15n/11 and 67n/49 for larger n, and that P(4) = 7, the first lower bounds above the trivial n, though all are linear and leave Naslund's superlinear question open. P(n) is the least r + s such that the tensor [x₁ = x₄][x₂ = x₃] on [n]⁴ is a sum of r tensors of rank one along one pairing of the coordinates and s along another; equivalently, the least rank B + rank R(C) over splittings of the swap matrix as B + C, with R the realignment. Naslund asked, as Problem 12 of his paper (arXiv 2017, JCTA 2020), whether P(n) ≥ n^(1 + ε). The repository proves P(n) ≥ 4n/3 for n ≥ 3, 15n/11 for n ≥ 5, 67n/49 for n ≥ 7, n + 3 for n ≥ 4, P(5) ≥ 8, P(6) ≥ 9 and P(4) = 7, with an exact-arithmetic script showing the border value at n = 4 is lower. The paper also shows that no argument of the slice kind used here can reach 2n. The README's account of the run says one agent posed the lower-bound question and proved the trivial bound unprompted, a second improved it, the operator then set the goal of going further, and the bounds above followed within about 74 minutes. Lab: AIM Intelligence. Model: Claude Fable 5.2 lead with Claude Opus 5.5 workers, in an in-house multi-agent harness. Verification: Formally verified. Autonomy: AI-led.

item.title: First letters read in the Herculaneum scroll PHerc. 211
item.description: A Vesuvius Challenge contestant's 3D ink-detection model, trained only on other scrolls, revealed 11 readable Greek letters in a 4 cm strip of PHerc. 211, a carbonised bookroll in the National Library of Naples, which the challenge's papyrology team read as including "and to the" followed by the start of a word that may mean "difference". PHerc. 211 is a bookroll about 17 cm tall. The challenge received 37 submissions on it from 15 contestants and teams, several on the same area, where crushed and broken layers make it hard to follow a single sheet. Aranke embedded scans of public scrolls with a self-supervised 3D DINO model to find the ink-bearing scrolls most like the unread ones, segmented three of them, and transferred predictions from the team's published 2 micrometre ink model and its released labels onto roughly 9 micrometre segments, checking and correcting the labels by hand. He trained a residual 3D U-Net reading 16 planes of native CT from scratch on those labels, continued on labelled surfaces from 12 other scrolls and fragments, and finished with a soft loss to preserve faint traces; no data from the competition scrolls was used. The papyrology team's reading, with some letters uncertain, begins with kai and tei, followed by diaph-, which may be diaphorai or a form of diapherein. Lab: Vesuvius Challenge. Model: Residual 3D U-Net ink model trained by the contestant, with a self-supervised 3D DINO model used to choose training scrolls. Verification: Author verified. Autonomy: AI-assisted.

item.title: An 8-regular graph of girth 7 on 768 vertices, below the previous record of 774
item.description: Claude agents working for Quantavane under Arhan Canli constructed an 8-regular graph of girth 7 on 768 vertices, verified in Lean by kernel computation and registered on Palomar, improving the best known upper bound on the order of an (8,7)-cage from the 774 listed in the House of Graphs table. A (k, g)-cage is a k-regular graph of girth g with as few vertices as possible. For (8, 7) the Moore bound gives at least 457 vertices, and published constructions gave 777 (Abreu, Araujo-Pardo, Balbuena, Labbate and Salas, 2015), 784 (Kiss, 2025) and 774 (Exoo, Goedgebeur, Jooken, Stubbe and Van den Eede, 2026). The new graph is the case q = 7 of a construction that starts from the incidence graph of the generalized quadrangle W(7), with 800 vertices, modifies Kiss's construction by deleting the lines of two rows, and repairs the vertices left one neighbour short with a matching, giving 800 - 16 - 16 = 768. Lean's kernel checks, by decide +kernel and without native_decide, that the adjacency lists define a simple 8-regular graph and that for every vertex the non-backtracking walks of length at most 3 through any two neighbours end in disjoint sets, which rules out cycles of length up to 6, and an explicit 7-cycle fixes the girth at exactly 7. Lab: Quantavane. Model: Claude (Anthropic) agents; version not stated. Verification: Formally verified. Autonomy: AI-led.

item.title: Green's Problem 64 proved in Lean: infinitely many primes p for which p-2 has an odd number of prime factors
item.description: GPT-6 Astra, in a repository run by Igor Inozemtsev, produced an 83-page proof and a Lean formalization, registered on Palomar, that infinitely many primes p have p-2 with an odd number of prime factors counted with multiplicity, Problem 64 on Ben Green's list of open problems, drawing on an October 2026 manuscript by Jizhou Guo that the agent consulted. Green's list notes that with p − 2 the question is a weak form of the twin prime conjecture: the integers with an odd number of prime factors have density one half, so it asks for infinitely many primes in a set of density one half, but the parity problem of sieve theory blocks the usual methods. Chen proved in 1966 that p + 2 has at most two prime factors infinitely often without deciding parity, and Pintz showed in 2010 that p + d has an odd number of prime factors infinitely often for at least one d among 2, 4, …, 16. The proof assigns weights to integers u in [x, 2x] with Ω(u) odd, sieves the values u + 2 using a shifted correlation estimate, and bounds the contribution of products of two large primes from above, leaving positive weight on primes for every large x. The Lean statement, written with Mathlib's Ω, is identical to Green64.green_64 in Google DeepMind's Formal Conjectures, where it is categorised as an open research problem. The project's timeline records the proof accepted by the Lean kernel, by nanoda and by con-ron on 142,651 declarations, and the full Palomar workflow passing in CI on 13 November. Lab: Independent. Model: GPT-6 Astra (OpenAI). Verification: Formally verified. Autonomy: AI-led.

item.title: Stepped-wedge randomised trial of AI-guided site selection for tuberculosis case-finding in Pakistan (SPOT-TB)
item.description: Across 3,936 screening camps and 269,254 people in all four provinces of Pakistan, mobile x-ray teams switched in random order from conventional site selection to locations recommended by the MATCH-AI software; tuberculosis yield per camp was 7% higher but not significantly so in the intention-to-treat analysis (adjusted risk ratio 1.07, 95% CI 0.94-1.22), and 32% higher in a per-protocol analysis of camps held within 5 km of a recommended site. The trial was embedded in community active case-finding run by Pakistan's National TB Control Program and private partners with Global Fund support. Thirty mobile x-ray van teams working in 68 districts were randomised to the time at which they moved from choosing camp sites by field knowledge, experience and historical data to sites recommended by MATCH-AI. Between 1 August 2023 and 28 September 2024 there were 2,046 control and 1,890 intervention camps. The primary outcome was the number of people diagnosed with bacteriologically confirmed tuberculosis per camp, analysed by intention to treat, with a validated per-protocol analysis restricted to camps within 5 km of an AI-recommended location. The trial is registered as NCT06017843 and was funded by the Gates Foundation and the Global Fund through Mercy Corps. Lab: Centre for Global Public Health, Pakistan. Model: MATCH-AI (Mapping and Analysis for Tailored disease Control and Health system strengthening) geographic targeting software. Verification: Peer reviewed. Autonomy: AI-assisted.

item.title: Talagrand's Ultimate Matching Conjecture proved for finite critical exponents and refuted at the endpoints
item.description: Three probabilists posted a 70-page proof, largely generated and proof-checked by language models, that random points in the unit square can be matched with simultaneous exponential tail bounds in both coordinates for every pair of finite critical exponents, settling Talagrand's Ultimate Matching Conjecture in that range, and showing that it fails at the two endpoint cases. Talagrand posed the conjecture as Research Problem 17.1.2 of his 2021 monograph: match N independent uniform points in the unit square to evenly spread points by a single permutation whose coordinate displacements obey exponential tail bounds of exponents α₁ and α₂ at once, at the scale √(log N/N), whenever 1/α₁ + 1/α₂ = 1/2. The paper proves this for all finite α₁, α₂ > 2, for an evenly spread deterministic target and for a second independent sample, by building on the flat torus a current whose divergence is Gaussian white noise projected on a dyadic grid and whose coordinates satisfy the critical anisotropic Orlicz bounds, then transferring it to a matching through an optimal-transport reduction. At the endpoints (2, ∞) and (∞, 2) a Brownian local-time construction shows that the normalised optimal cost diverges, so the conjecture is false there. Exact endpoint asymptotics are claimed only in a separate file in the authors' repository. Lab: Independent (CNRS and Université Gustave Eiffel; University of Pisa). Model: GPT-6 (OpenAI) and Claude Fable (Anthropic); versions not stated. Verification: Claimed. Autonomy: Collaborative.

item.title: Smale's mean value constant shown to equal 4, with a Lean proof
item.description: Dave Goel, steering Claude and ChatGPT in alternation, proved that the supremum over all degrees of Smale's mean value constant is exactly 4, Smale's own 1981 bound, approached as the degree grows but never attained, so no smaller constant works for every degree; the main theorem is registered on Palomar as a Lean proof. For a complex polynomial p of degree d ≥ 2 with p(0) = 0 and p′(0) ≠ 0, let S(p) be the least value of |p(c)/(c p′(0))| over the critical points c, and let K(d) be the supremum of S(p) in degree d. Smale proved K(d) ≤ 4 in 1981 and asked whether 4 could be replaced by 1. That conjecture was refuted earlier in 2026, which this registry records at 2026-09-03-smale-mean-value-k1, and lower bounds then rose to 1.1018 (Jatar and Ng) and 1.1559 (Goel), with Jatar and Ng listing whether the supremum K^* equals 4 as open. The paper proves K^* = lim_(d → ∞) K(d) = 4 by combining Jatar and Ng's reduction to admissible univalent Blaschke pairs with an explicit construction. Since each K(d) is known to be below 4, the supremum is not attained. The Lean development proves the main theorem in the paper's normalization together with Smale's bound K(d) ≤ 4, that K(d) does not decrease with d, and that K(d) < 4 in every degree. Lab: Independent. Model: Claude (Anthropic) and ChatGPT (OpenAI), alternated; versions not stated. Verification: Formally verified. Autonomy: Collaborative.

item.title: Large triangles in planar sets of positive upper density, resolving Castro-Silva's conjecture, with a Lean proof
item.description: Polona Durcik directed GPT-6 Astra Pro to a proof, formalized in Lean by Claude Opus 5.5 and registered on Palomar, that every measurable planar set of positive upper Banach density contains a rotated and translated copy of every sufficiently large dilate of any fixed non-degenerate triangle, which gives the planar conjecture of Davi Castro-Silva. Furstenberg, Katznelson and Weiss showed that every positive-radius neighbourhood of a set of positive upper density contains congruent copies of all large dilates of a triangle, Bourgain obtained exact copies of non-degenerate simplices in dimension three and higher, and Falconer, Kovac and Yavicoli reached the planar statement for density above one half. Castro-Silva conjectured it for every positive upper density, measured in squares centred at the origin. The note proves it under upper Banach density, which dominates that centred density, and with orientation-preserving copies, so it implies the conjecture. The argument combines the density Hales-Jewett theorem with an operator-norm continuity estimate for the triangle-counting form, derived from a trilinear smoothing theorem. Its provenance statement says the manuscript came from three conversations with GPT-6 Astra Pro on 4 and 5 November 2026, in which Durcik directed the model toward trilinear oscillatory integral methods from papers by Christ and by Christ, Durcik and Roos that she supplied, with otherwise generic prompts. Lab: Independent. Model: GPT-6 Astra Pro via Codex (proof and manuscript); Claude Opus 5.5 at medium effort (Lean formalization). Verification: Formally verified. Autonomy: AI-led.

item.title: Lean-checked proof of the Aaronson-Ambainis conjecture on influential variables of bounded polynomials
item.description: A research system at Physical Superintelligence running a non-public Anthropic model produced a proof, checked in Lean by two independent kernels, that every low-degree polynomial bounded on the Boolean cube with non-trivial variance has a variable of polynomially large influence, the conjecture Aaronson and Ambainis showed implies that quantum query algorithms can be simulated classically on most inputs with polynomially more queries. The main theorem says that every f:{−1, 1}ⁿ → [−1, 1] of degree at most d has a coordinate j with Infⱼ(f) ≥ √15/500π⁴Var(f)^(5/2)/d⁶, which in the conjecture's own normalisation gives an influence of at least (ε/d)⁷, where Aaronson and Ambainis asked only for (ε/d)^(O(1)). The proof follows a plan of Lovett and Zhang through level sets and fractional certificates and replaces the inequality their plan left as a conjecture with a new all-pairs inequality, obtained from a bijection produced by the lowest-degree terms of a determinant and related to Reimer's butterfly lemma; a row bound by the method of Agarwal and Ben-David supplies the degree dependence. The Lean statement of record, PrintedConjecture, sits in a file that imports only Mathlib and uses no definition of the project. For each of the four final theorems the repository records an axiom print of exactly propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound, a kernel replay with leanchecker from an empty environment, the same replays with the independent lean4lean checker, and a sandboxed Comparator run that also rechecks the proofs with nanoda. Lab: Physical Superintelligence (PSI). Model: Non-public Anthropic model, run in a research harness built at PSI. Verification: Formally verified. Autonomy: AI-led.

item.title: OpenAI reports 81 high-severity Firefox vulnerabilities and 948 Linux kernel privilege-escalation exploits found by its models
item.description: OpenAI announced that its restricted GPT-6 Cyber model found 81 previously unknown high-severity Firefox vulnerabilities, and that an automated pipeline found 2,308 candidate Linux kernel flaws, reproduced 1,724 and produced local privilege-escalation exploits for 948; Mozilla's advisories credit dozens of high-impact Firefox CVEs to OpenAI reporters, while no CVEs are public for the Linux results. According to BleepingComputer's report of the announcement, GPT-6 Cyber found 81 previously unknown high-severity vulnerabilities in Firefox and helped develop patches, many already released by Mozilla, and in separate Linux kernel research identified 2,308 potential flaws, reproduced 1,724 and developed local privilege-escalation exploits for 948 distinct vulnerabilities that could let an unprivileged user gain root. OpenAI also reported 48.5% exploit success on its ExploitGym benchmark against 32.1% for GPT-5.6 Cyber, rated the model Critical for cybersecurity under its Preparedness Framework, and restricted access to customers of its Daybreak Red programme. Mozilla's advisory for Firefox 160, published on 10 November 2026, lists 99 CVEs, of which 26, all rated high impact, credit OpenAI or Amy Burnett of OpenAI as reporter; its Firefox ESR 153.6 advisory of 27 October credits 33. Lab: OpenAI. Model: GPT-6 Cyber, available only to approved customers, per coverage; OpenAI's own posts could not be read. Verification: Claimed. Autonomy: Search scaffold.

item.title: Randomised implementation study of CT-based AI risk support for cystic renal masses (KITE-CRM)
item.description: Among 5,869 adults randomised at one Shanghai hospital to AI-assisted or standard CT reporting, benign pathology was found in 16.4% of treated lesions with AI support against 40.3% with standard care, after the model reached external AUROCs of 0.913 to 0.999 at five hospitals and raised six radiologists' AUROC from 0.825 to 0.973 in a reader study; in the subgroup of cystic masses the tool is built for, the difference was not significant. Cystic renal masses are often overtreated. The model was developed on 570 training cases from one referral centre (2020-2021), validated internally on 235 and externally on 528 cases from five hospitals (2022-2025), with one index lesion per patient and a fixed decision threshold. In a randomised crossover reader study six radiologists read 117 external cases with and without AI, and assistance cut mean reading time from 9.7 to 5.5 minutes. From November 2025 to February 2026, 5,869 consecutive adults having contrast-enhanced abdominal CT at Changhai Hospital were randomised 1:1 to AI-assisted (2,934) or standard reporting (2,935), with the proportion of pathologically benign lesions among treated lesions as the primary clinical endpoint. In a post hoc intention-to-treat analysis benign intervention occurred in 0.95% against 3.54% of randomised participants. The trial is registered with the Chinese Clinical Trial Registry as ChiCTR2500112290 and the model code is public. Lab: Changhai Hospital, Naval Medical University. Model: KITE-CRM (Kidney Imaging-based Triage Engine for Cystic Renal Masses), a deep-learning model on corticomedullary-phase CT. Verification: Peer reviewed. Autonomy: AI-assisted.

item.title: Limit free energy of the Hopfield model identified at every temperature and loading ratio
item.description: Six mathematicians identified, by a Parisi-type variational formula, the limit of the free energy of the Hopfield associative-memory model with random Bernoulli patterns at every temperature and every ratio of patterns to neurons, after one of them obtained the existence of the limit with assistance from GPT 6 Astra. In the Hopfield model, spins interact through independent random patterns, and in the regime where the number of patterns grows in proportion to the number of spins, Amit, Gutfreund and Sompolinsky derived a non-rigorous phase diagram in the 1980s; rigorous results covered high temperature, small loading with low temperature, or assumed concentration of the order parameters. The paper proves that the expected free energy converges for every loading ratio and inverse temperature and identifies the limit as a sup-inf variational formula of Parisi type, with almost sure and L¹ convergence as well. A Hubbard-Stratonovich transformation turns the model into a bipartite spin glass with ±1 and spherical spins, which the authors show is equivalent to one with Gaussian patterns plus finitely many Bernoulli random fields, and they solve that model by adapting recent techniques for spin glasses. The statement of AI use says Ayman Ali obtained the existence proof with assistance from GPT 6 Astra and shared it, that Chen and Mourrat already had a detailed draft identifying the limit for Gaussian patterns, and that all six wrote the final manuscript with GPT 6 Astra and Fable 5.1. Lab: Independent (Hebrew University, MIT, NYU Shanghai, Weizmann Institute, Sorbonne University, ENS Lyon). Model: GPT 6 Astra (existence proof and writing) and Fable 5.1 (writing). Verification: Author verified. Autonomy: AI-assisted.

item.title: AI against clinician left-ventricular segmentation of cardiac MRI for predicting mortality in 27,382 patients
item.description: In 27,382 patients scanned at Barts Heart Centre in London and the University of Pittsburgh Medical Center and followed for a median 5.6 years, ejection fraction measured by deep-learning segmentation of cardiac MRI predicted death slightly better than the clinicians' own measurements (C index 0.669 against 0.637), a gap that shrank to 0.781 against 0.777 after adjustment for age and sex. The cohort combined 26,106 consecutive patients scanned at Barts Heart Centre between October 2014 and December 2019, referred from nine hospitals, with 1,276 scanned at UPMC between June 2010 and March 2016; 3,458 (13%) died during follow-up. AI segmentation was run on every scan and Cox models compared the prognostic value of AI-measured and clinician-measured left-ventricular volumes. AI ejection fraction gave better model fit (a difference in AIC of 161) and slightly better discrimination (a difference in C index of 0.033, 95% CI 0.026-0.041), and adding it to the clinician measurement improved fit. The authors conclude that AI could be used for first-line measurement of ejection fraction with clinician oversight, and that this should be tested prospectively. Lab: University College London. Model: Deep-learning left-ventricular segmentation of cardiac MRI, not named in the abstract. Verification: Peer reviewed. Autonomy: AI-assisted.

item.title: Longitudinal study finds DAX Copilot did not make primary care clinicians more efficient at Atrium Health
